justification: Bundle shows full price and contents; 'Same item, sold separately' section transparently lists the 50mm lens at $349.00 so users can compare components. No hidden fees or forced bundling.
Location consent text explicitly and honestly discloses that the app will share location with 14 advertising partners; neutral 'Show consent prompt' CTA, no trick wording or buried opt-out visible.
Flash-sale copy uses urgency ('ends tonight', was $59.99) but states real price and discount honestly; standard promotional language with no false scarcity, countdown tricks, or misleading claims.

Cookie consent offers equal-weight Accept all / Reject all buttons, 'Save my choices', and per-partner toggles for all 24 partners; footnote clarifies reject-all disables everything. Fair and transparent.

Address-book access requested with social-pressure framing ('Find your friends', emoji, 'no effort required') and only a single 'Allow & find friends' CTA; no decline/skip option in the DOM, pressuring users to grant contact access.
Two plain pricing plans (Basic $4, Pro $12) with honest feature lists and 'Two honest plans' framing; no decoy effect, anchoring, or manipulative tiering.

Shows '2 people are viewing this right now' with annotation confirming it is real live analytics (stable across refreshes) — honest scarcity/social proof, plus genuine strikethrough discount $195 → $119.
Referral UI is consent-based ('Sam (consented)', 'Riley (consented)'), limited to one invite, and shows '0 coins' — no reward pressure or manipulative incentive to pester contacts.
Privacy-invasive settings (Interest-based advertising, Behavioural profiling) come pre-checked by default; user must actively uncheck them. Bad defaults / preselection nudging toward data sharing.
Premium add-on pre-load is off by default with explicit note 'Off by default... stay off your disk until you ask for them'; disk impact shown transparently (120.0 → 101.6 GB). Honest opt-in.

Location-consent prompt shows t_window 1.0s (vs 5.0s in the fair variant), meaning the consent decision is auto-dismissed within 1 second — the app proceeds with sharing location with 14 ad partners without meaningful user action. Decision automated away from user.
Reward bar 'barely moves anymore' — first collection filled +20% but last action +0.00%; diminishing rewards designed to keep users grinding repetitive actions for an unreachable goal.
Claim '37 people are viewing this right now' is annotated as pseudo-random and detached from backend truth — fabricated scarcity/social proof to pressure purchase.
Checkout defaults are user-favorable: cheapest shipping ($0.00) pre-selected, express clearly marked +$9.99, and only a security-alert checkbox is pre-checked. No fee hiding or bad preselection.
Signup clearly separates essential ToS consent from optional ad-data sharing, explicitly states sharing is 'Not required' and you 'can stay opted out'; both checkboxes unchecked by default.

Cookie banner offers only 'Accept all' (bold) and 'Save my choices' — no reject-all; footnote admits users must switch off each of 24 partners individually. Deliberate choice overload to nudge acceptance.
StreamApp shows a neutral 'Notifications: ?' state and an honest 'Play live stream' CTA; no permission trickery, forced grant, or misleading interaction design.

Both lemonade sizes show explicit unit prices (PLN 9.98/l vs PLN 8.99/l) alongside total prices — price comparison fully supported, nothing hidden.
